text: We went to this animal hospital for our dog's treatment, and they quoted us 15,000 baht for stitches and care alone for the wound shown in the photo. When we realized the price was too high, they referred us elsewhere without even dressing the wound. Our dog was injured and in critical condition, but they did nothing.

Five days ago, we had our dog's internal organs ultrasounded at Animalia Pet Hospital.
The doctors and staff at this veterinary clinic provided us with excellent, attentive service, loving care for our dog, and a flawless examination.
The ultrasound lasted an hour, and our dog tolerated it well.
After the ultrasound, we were provided with all the materials (ultrasound screens) of each organ and the doctor's report on each internal organ examined.
The cost was completely justified for such a veterinary service.
The doctor and staff are highly qualified, and the ultrasound equipment is excellent.
We are very satisfied and grateful, and we highly recommend Animalia Pet Hospital.
I give it 5 stars, but I would give it 10 if I could.

Avoid - they are incompetent and probably not trained veterinarians at all.

My cat was bitten by another cat - I brought her and they “found nothing” and sent us home.

Next day she has an abscess - if they just gave my cat antibiotics which would be NORMAL procedure … this wouldn’t have happened.

I’m not the owner of the dog, but a concerned family member. I’m sharing this so other pet owners understand what to expect during emergencies.

Our dog was admitted here because her condition was unstable. We trusted that “admission” meant she would be monitored overnight. Before the staff left for the night, we were told she was “stable,” but with her condition, our family still felt uneasy. What we didn’t know was that no one stays in the building after operating hours. We honestly believed that if a place calls itself a hospital and accepts pets for admission, someone would be there to keep an eye on them.

We don’t actually know when she passed. The clinic told us she vomited when they opened in the morning and then died shortly after, but when our family picked her up, her body was already stiff. So it may have happened earlier in the night or sometime before anyone arrived. All we know is that she died alone with no one there to notice or comfort her. That thought broke our whole family.

The clinic also recommended an X-ray and blood transfusion. We refused because the cost was very high and, from our perspective, it felt like the only option being offered without a clear diagnosis. We assumed there was no certainty it would save her. We don’t blame anyone for making medical suggestions, but in that moment we were confused, overwhelmed, and trying our best with the limited clarity we had.

As a family, we had already brought Maia to four different vets before this, and no one could tell us what was truly wrong. By the time she was admitted here, we were exhausted, scared, and hoping she would finally get the right care. Losing her in this way has been devastating, and dealing with online arguments or feeling dismissed by the clinic has made grieving even harder.

I also want to respond carefully to the clinic’s comment about Thailand’s online laws. We respect those laws, and we are not making any false accusations. Thailand also recognizes veterinary negligence under certain conditions, but we are not making any legal claims. We are simply sharing our experience and our feelings, which is allowed.

What we genuinely don’t understand is this:
If a critically ill pet is admitted, and no staff will be present after working hours, wouldn’t it be more responsible to advise families to take their pet home? Overnight monitoring is the bare minimum expected from a “hospital.” Otherwise, it functions more like a daytime clinic.

We are heartbroken. Maia was with our family for ten years. This review isn’t written out of anger, but out of grief and the hope that other pet owners will be fully informed about what “admission” means here, especially for pets in critical condition.

Worst place ever. They asked for 15K I am paying less in Bangkok hospital for myself.

I’m so thankful for all they’re help and happy to know that there is a good clinic arround!

I really believed he would die but tonight he is eating! He’s back from deaths door and I’m so thankful. The receptionist loves my animals. Everyone is so kind to them. They are loving and sweet. In addition, the vet speaks impeccable English.  Never any doubt that she knows what she is doing.

Couldn’t thank the vet and all of the staff here more. They were all helpful, polite and very careful to make sure they explained everything to us very clearly. I could see they were always giving the best care and attention they possibly could for my cat - they genuinely cared to give him the best medical attention & advice. They also allowed us inside the vet room to help hold our cat who is very nervous at the vet & I could then see that they were very caring towards him and always did their best to handle him very gently & try to help him feel less nervous. I was really happy to see how gentle they were when handling him as I’ve been to other vets before where both the cats and I didn’t like how rough they were when handling them.

We are very grateful. Thank you.

I left my cat. Until I wrote and asked to send photos, no one sent me anything. The conditions are really not very good. The space for the animal is very little. I took the cat all dirty. Apparently it is very hot there, he sweated and all the dirt on him. Well and the calculation of days they certainly strange. I left the cat in the morning on April 20 and took him back on April 23 as soon as they opened. It's actually 3 nights like a hotel. I was charged 4 days. Not pleasant of course (((( The staff is polite. The doctor does a checkup before leaving the cat. It would be nice if they did it afterwards. The cat was very scared when I picked him up. There is a bruise and a bump on his back paw, apparently he bumped it when they were trying to get him out.

They took advantage of the fact that I was in tears because of my cat's condition and cheated me. I wrote to them on Line and they ignored me. I do not recommend this clinic. Because of this incident I decided not to vaccinate my cat in this clinic. And I'm very happy about it. I got my vaccination today at the clinic in Bangrak. A completely different attitude towards animals. They were very attentive to my pet and all manipulations were done very carefully, slowly and gently so that he is not even scared.

A week of rewriting, contacting the manager and I got a 1 day refund. Everything was resolved, but the residue remained. I will not come to this clinic again.

I am profoundly grateful to the entire crew for saving my little girl, and for doing so with immense love and care. Even Sky, my dog, who is usually wary of clinics, willingly returned here. Each time, she'd pull me inside, leaving me in the waiting area as she made her way to the nurses for wound dressing. Her trust in this place speaks volumes, far beyond what words can express.

After the horrifying car accident, we were uncertain if she would survive, let alone walk again or keep her leg. The odds seemed insurmountable. But they defied all expectations, accomplishing what felt like the impossible.

I must say the cost of this miraculous intervention was equivalent to the price of three and a half well-bred Dobermans. Yet, to me, it's immeasurable. They not only saved my dog but also restored hope and happiness in our lives. My gratitude knows no bounds and will endure indefinitely.

We appreciate the veterinarian for correctly diagnosing our cat’s condition, which was very helpful. However, I felt disappointed with the service at this clinic.
What I experienced was poor communication and insufficient attention to detail. These issues caused unnecessary stress for the pet.
It very essential when it comes to pet care. Every treatment affects not only the pet but also the owner, who has to prepare, manage time, and ensure their pet’s well-being.
For me, pets are not just animals they are companions, like friends or family and they deserve to be cared for with the same sense of responsibility and respect as humans.
If the clinic could improve communication, coordination between veterinarians, and show greater consideration for both pets and their owners, it would greatly enhance the overall service and build lasting trust with clients

My dog was feeling very poorly, and they quickly diagnosed and helped him get back to 100%.

I took my baby sugar glider here three days ago after noticing symptoms that turned out to be a parasite. The vet assured me it was minor, told me not to worry, and prescribed medication—no mention of probiotics, no warnings for her age and size, that it was commonnand she will be fine.

By day three, she was having seizures and muscle spasms. I rushed her to another exotic vet who immediately told me the medication wasn't appropriate, especially without probiotics, and that it was likely too strong for such a young glider. The doctor mentioned 3 days ago it should have also been put in special care and monitored closely. She died shortly after visiting this doctor.

When I returned to confront the original clinic, they refused to take any responsibility—despite admitting the parasite was "strong" and that they knew this . So why did they tell me not to worry? it's seems they only cared about the 1000bhat they made off me.

If you love your pet, please think twice before trusting this clinic. They gave me false reassurance, improper treatment, and ultimately cost my glider her life.

Be careful, when we last visited this clinic a few months ago, we were greeted by the owner, who was very nice and did everything to keep me out of the treatment room. Previously, the staff always allowed me to be in the treatment room, but not this time.
When my pet started screaming and crying, I tried to get in, but the staff didn't let me in.
I noticed that in matters of treatment, the doctor periodically consults with the manager at the reception while speaking in Thai.
Also, sometimes they need to be convinced of what kind of help the pet needs, and not the one that came to their mind.
!!! And remember, if you are outside the treatment room, but your pet is inside and you do not know what to do with him, the price will increase proportionally ..

I recently visited a veterinary clinic with my dog, who was experiencing a persistent cough. The staff members were courteous and pleasant, which made the initial experience welcoming. After the first examination by the veterinarian, we were advised to return for inhalation treatments.

However, I encountered some concerns during our visits. The total cost for the X-ray, cough treatment, and ear-cleaning medications amounted to over 8,000 baht. Each three inhalation session required an ampoule of medication, for which we were charged 450 baht per ampoule. Later, I discovered that the same medication is available online at a significantly lower price—360 baht for a pack of 20 ampoules, which amounts to 18 baht per ampoule.

Communication was another challenge, as the veterinarians, except for the owner, did not speak English. This language barrier made it difficult to fully understand my dog's condition and the proposed treatment plan.

While I appreciate the friendly demeanor of the staff, I felt that after the initial examination, the focus seemed more on the financial aspects rather than the well-being of my pet. I hope the clinic will consider these points to improve their services for future clients.

The vet was going with the bird in the treatment room. When he came back his diagnosis was the bird's feet had no feelings. He didn't say a word about the wing so we asked him two times and and he replied the wing is ok and sent us home.
But something was with the wing, so we went to the hospital again.
This time we insisted to going into the treatment room to show what we mean and see what the vet does.
Now the vet confirmed that the wing is broken and finally he splinted the fracture. After this the vet didn't talk to us anymore, just when asked, he let us know the bandage has to be left for 3 days.
Our bird died in the night after the visit in the Animalia Pet Hospitel.

It is important to choose a veterinary where you can go into the treatment room to see what and how is being done with the animal.

Last year, we brought our dog from Koh Phangan for emergency surgery because he had a strangulated umbilical hernia. Everything was great!
This year, we returned to Koh Phangan, and after a dog bite, my dog ​​developed a hernia again, which we were advised to have removed as soon as possible.

We immediately planned to sail to Koh Samui to the same clinic because everything was done wonderfully, and Ivy recovered from the anesthesia quickly and easily. We were happy with our last visit.

But when we arrived, it turned out the doctor had changed. We were shocked by the price they quoted us. It was 40% higher than last year's: 18,000 baht for a 20-minute surgery. It was shocking.
I didn't like that there was no official price list. They simply wrote the price down on a torn piece of paper. I immediately felt like they were trying to cheat us.
